meta.title: 3D Bioprinted Human Cortical Neural Constructs Derived from Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: A custom coaxial microfluidic extrusion printer built layered meshes of hiPSC-derived cortical neurons and glia in alginate/Matrigel fibres. Constructs stayed partly viable and functional up to 50 days after printing.

formulations.review_notes: Speed converted from 240 mm/min. Viability measured on one construct (nine fields).
formulations.name: 2% alginate + 0.5x Matrigel microfibres
formulations.composition_detail: 2% w/v alginate + 0.5x Matrigel, crosslinked with 0.33 mM CaCl2, then alginate lyase
formulations.key_outcome: Printed hiPSC cortical constructs stayed 68% viable 50 days after printing.

evidence.quote: We obtained the best results using a solution containing 2% w/v alginate and 0.5× Matrigel (~50% dilution from stock), printed using 0.33 mM CaCl2 crosslinking solution
deposited at a speed of 240 mm/min
viability was consistently maintained over time as assessed by live/dead staining up to DPP50 (68 ± 8% live cells
